pricing_unit.summary: Revenue scales with the data the customer touches, so usage forecasts decide whether the deal looks healthy.

core_competitive_threats: Legacy data silos that nobody wants to migrate
cluster_objections: Our warehouse already has vector search. Why add another meter to our bill?
Consumption is hard to forecast. How do we keep credits from spiking at quarter close?

cards.title: Where it sits
cards.body: Data, context and memory platforms feed models the right information at the right time.

cards.title: What the customer pays for
cards.body: Pure consumption. The customer pays only for what they use.

cards.title: How the money works
cards.body: Revenue lands only when queries run. Signing is halftime: the second half is getting usage to ramp.

cards.title: What threatens the deal
cards.body: Legacy data silos nobody wants to migrate, and good-enough native cloud databases.

quiz.prompt: When does a pure consumption deal make money?
quiz.why: With pure consumption, revenue follows usage, not the contract.

quiz.prompt: What is the second half of a consumption sale?
quiz.why: Close the deal, then close the consumption.

quiz.prompt: Which threat keeps data where it is?
quiz.why: Migration effort is the biggest reason buyers stay put.
